# Proposal: add-book-catalog

## Why

The library-loans service needs a catalogue before anything can be lent: librarians must be able to register the
books the library owns and see which copies exist. This first change also fixes the service's architecture, so every
later change has a stated structure to follow.

## What Changes

- Register a book (ISBN, title, author, number of copies); reject an invalid ISBN and a duplicate ISBN.
- List the catalogue, ordered by title.
- An HTTP-style inbound adapter for both operations and an in-memory store for books.
- The service's hexagonal architecture is stated in `design.md` (## Architecture) and becomes the DaedalusArch spec.

## Capabilities

### New Capabilities
- `book-catalog`: registering books and listing the catalogue.

### Modified Capabilities

## Impact

- New code under `src/` (domain, application, adapters, config). No external dependency.
- `.daedalus/architecture.yaml` is generated from this change's design.

# Spec Delta

## Purpose

Lets librarians register the books the library owns and list the catalogue, so copies can later be lent.

## ADDED Requirements

### Requirement: Register a book
The system SHALL register a book with an ISBN-13, a title, an author and a number of copies of at least one, and
SHALL reject an ISBN that is not a valid ISBN-13 or that is already registered.

#### Scenario: Valid book is registered
- **WHEN** a librarian registers ISBN 9780132350884, "Clean Code", "Robert C. Martin", 2 copies
- **THEN** the book is in the catalogue with 2 copies

#### Scenario: Invalid ISBN is rejected
- **WHEN** a librarian registers ISBN 9780132350880
- **THEN** the request fails with an invalid-ISBN error and the catalogue is unchanged

#### Scenario: Duplicate ISBN is rejected
- **WHEN** a librarian registers an ISBN that is already in the catalogue
- **THEN** the request fails with a duplicate-book error

### Requirement: List the catalogue
The system SHALL list every registered book with its ISBN, title, author and copies, ordered by title.

#### Scenario: Catalogue is listed by title
- **WHEN** "Refactoring" and "Clean Code" are registered and the catalogue is listed
- **THEN** "Clean Code" comes before "Refactoring"

# Design: add-book-catalog

## Context

First change of the service; there is no code yet. See proposal.md for the motivation. The service must run without
any external dependency, so persistence is in memory and the transport is a minimal HTTP-style request/response pair.

## Goals / Non-Goals

**Goals:**
- Fix the architecture every later change follows, in a form a tool can check.
- Keep business rules (ISBN validity, copies >= 1) in the domain, independent of transport and storage.

**Non-Goals:**
- A real HTTP server or database.

## Architecture

Style: hexagonal

### Layers

| Layer | Kind | Directories | Roles |
|---|---|---|---|
| domain | domain | `src/domain/**` | entity, value-object, domain-service |
| application | application | `src/application/**` | use-case, port |
| adapters-inbound | presentation | `src/adapters/inbound/**` | controller |
| adapters-outbound | infrastructure | `src/adapters/outbound/**` | repository, gateway |
| config | application | `src/config/**` | composition-root |

### Allowed dependencies

- application -> domain
- adapters-inbound -> application, domain
- adapters-outbound -> application, domain
- config -> domain, application, adapters-inbound, adapters-outbound

### Forbidden in domain

- `express`
- `@nestjs/*`
- `typeorm`
- `prisma`
- `@prisma/*`
- `pg`

## Decisions

- **Ports in the application layer** (`src/application/ports/`): the use cases own the interfaces they need
  (`BookRepository`); the outbound adapter implements them. Alternative: ports in the domain. Rejected because the
  ports here are use-case driven, not domain concepts.
- **Isbn value object** validates the ISBN-13 check digit in its factory, so an invalid ISBN cannot exist in the
  domain.
- **Inbound adapter without a framework**: `BookController` maps an `HttpRequest` to a use case and the result to an
  `HttpResponse` (status, body). Errors from the domain map to 400 and 409.
- **Composition root** (`src/config/container.ts`) is the only place that instantiates adapters.

## Risks / Trade-offs

- [In-memory store loses data on restart] → acceptable for the demo; the port keeps a real store a one-file change.

# Tasks

## 1. Domain

- [ ] 1.1 `Isbn` value object with ISBN-13 check-digit validation
- [ ] 1.2 `Book` entity (isbn, title, author, copies >= 1) and domain errors

## 2. Application

- [ ] 2.1 `BookRepository` port (save, findByIsbn, findAll)
- [ ] 2.2 `RegisterBookUseCase` (rejects duplicates) and `ListBooksUseCase` (ordered by title)

## 3. Adapters and wiring

- [ ] 3.1 `InMemoryBookRepository` implementing the port
- [ ] 3.2 HTTP-style types and `BookController` (POST /books, GET /books)
- [ ] 3.3 Composition root `container.ts`

rules.name: dependency-direction-graph
rules.description: dependency-direction-graph
rules.construct: Dependency rule over the allowed-dependency graph (adapters depend on ports, never the reverse)
rules.source: Cockburn, "Hexagonal Architecture" (2005). The application core communicates with the outside only through ports. It does not depend on adapters, UI or databases.

rules.name: no-cyclic-deps
rules.description: Detects simple circular import/re-export chains of length 2..10 (one row per cycle with its first-edge target and line, FR-12; row 101 is a truncation sentinel)
rules.source: Martin 2017, ch. 14 "Component Coupling", ADP. The component dependency graph has no cycles. (Clean row; the Hexagonal preset composes it)

rules.name: layer-skip-graph
rules.description: layer-skip-graph
rules.construct: No sideways step between layers with no allowed dependency
rules.source: Cockburn 2005 (adapters talk to the core, not to each other); rule-tiers.md: hexagonal does not define strict layering

rules.name: core-isolation
rules.description: core-isolation
rules.construct: Core isolation: the core depends on no adapter, UI or database
rules.source: Cockburn, "Hexagonal Architecture" (2005). The application core communicates with the outside only through ports. It does not depend on adapters, UI or databases.

rules.name: domain-purity
rules.description: Detects domain files importing or re-exporting forbidden framework/infrastructure packages (Package nodes, FR-11)
rules.source: Martin 2017, ch. 22; ch. 32 "Frameworks are details". Entities and use cases do not depend on frameworks, databases or the UI. (Clean row; the Hexagonal preset composes it)

rules.name: port-dependency-inversion
rules.description: port-dependency-inversion
rules.construct: Use cases depend on ports (ratio proxy)
rules.source: Martin 2017, ch. 11 "DIP"; Cockburn 2005 (a ratio with a threshold, so a proxy)

rules.name: port-adapter-pattern
rules.description: port-adapter-pattern
rules.construct: Driven adapters implement ports the core or application declares
rules.source: Cockburn 2005. Each external actor talks to the application through a port. Adapters convert between the port and the technology; secondary (driven) adapters implement ports the core defines.

rules.name: domain-state-purity
rules.description: Detects domain classes that hold infrastructure state through a field (FLOWS_TO) or an injected constructor parameter (CONSTRUCTOR_INJECTS)
rules.construct: Core isolation of state: the domain holds no infrastructure object
rules.source: Martin 2017, ch. 22 (the Dependency Rule; entities hold no outer-circle state); rule-tiers.md "Core isolation of state"

rules.description: Detects files with excessive outgoing dependencies

rules.name: component-instability

# Design: add-book-catalog

## Context

First change of the service; there is no code yet. See proposal.md for the motivation. The service must run without
any external dependency, so persistence is in memory and the transport is a minimal HTTP-style request/response pair.

## Goals / Non-Goals

**Goals:**
- Fix the architecture every later change follows, in a form a tool can check.
- Keep business rules (ISBN validity, copies >= 1) in the domain, independent of transport and storage.

**Non-Goals:**
- A real HTTP server or database.

## Architecture

Style: hexagonal

### Layers

| Layer | Kind | Directories | Roles |
|---|---|---|---|
| domain | domain | `src/domain/**` | entity, value-object, domain-service |
| application | application | `src/application/**` | use-case, port |
| adapters-inbound | presentation | `src/adapters/inbound/**` | controller |
| adapters-outbound | infrastructure | `src/adapters/outbound/**` | repository, gateway |
| config | application | `src/config/**` | composition-root |

### Allowed dependencies

- application -> domain
- adapters-inbound -> application, domain
- adapters-outbound -> application, domain
- config -> domain, application, adapters-inbound, adapters-outbound

### Forbidden in domain

- `express`
- `@nestjs/*`
- `typeorm`
- `prisma`
- `@prisma/*`
- `pg`

## Decisions

- **Ports in the application layer** (`src/application/ports/`): the use cases own the interfaces they need
  (`BookRepository`); the outbound adapter implements them. Alternative: ports in the domain. Rejected because the
  ports here are use-case driven, not domain concepts.
- **Isbn value object** validates the ISBN-13 check digit in its factory, so an invalid ISBN cannot exist in the
  domain.
- **Inbound adapter without a framework**: `BookController` maps an `HttpRequest` to a use case and the result to an
  `HttpResponse` (status, body). Errors from the domain map to 400 and 409.
- **Composition root** (`src/config/container.ts`) is the only place that instantiates adapters.

## Risks / Trade-offs

- [In-memory store loses data on restart] → acceptable for the demo; the port keeps a real store a one-file change.

# Proposal: add-book-catalog

## Why

The library-loans service needs a catalogue before anything can be lent: librarians must be able to register the
books the library owns and see which copies exist. This first change also fixes the service's architecture, so every
later change has a stated structure to follow.

## What Changes

- Register a book (ISBN, title, author, number of copies); reject an invalid ISBN and a duplicate ISBN.
- List the catalogue, ordered by title.
- An HTTP-style inbound adapter for both operations and an in-memory store for books.
- The service's hexagonal architecture is stated in `design.md` (## Architecture) and becomes the DaedalusArch spec.

## Capabilities

### New Capabilities
- `book-catalog`: registering books and listing the catalogue.

### Modified Capabilities

## Impact

- New code under `src/` (domain, application, adapters, config). No external dependency.
- `.daedalus/architecture.yaml` is generated from this change's design.

# Spec Delta

## Purpose

Lets librarians register the books the library owns and list the catalogue, so copies can later be lent.

## ADDED Requirements

### Requirement: Register a book
The system SHALL register a book with an ISBN-13, a title, an author and a number of copies of at least one, and
SHALL reject an ISBN that is not a valid ISBN-13 or that is already registered.

#### Scenario: Valid book is registered
- **WHEN** a librarian registers ISBN 9780132350884, "Clean Code", "Robert C. Martin", 2 copies
- **THEN** the book is in the catalogue with 2 copies

#### Scenario: Invalid ISBN is rejected
- **WHEN** a librarian registers ISBN 9780132350880
- **THEN** the request fails with an invalid-ISBN error and the catalogue is unchanged

#### Scenario: Duplicate ISBN is rejected
- **WHEN** a librarian registers an ISBN that is already in the catalogue
- **THEN** the request fails with a duplicate-book error

### Requirement: List the catalogue
The system SHALL list every registered book with its ISBN, title, author and copies, ordered by title.

#### Scenario: Catalogue is listed by title
- **WHEN** "Refactoring" and "Clean Code" are registered and the catalogue is listed
- **THEN** "Clean Code" comes before "Refactoring"

## Why

The service exists to lend books. With books and members in place, librarians need to record a loan, its due date,
and its return, and the system must stop a loan that would break the rules (no copy left, member at the limit).

## What Changes

- Lend a book to a member for 21 days; refuse when no copy is available or the member has reached the limit.
- Return a loan; a loan cannot be returned twice.
- List a member's open loans.

## Capabilities

### New Capabilities
- `lending`: lending, returning and listing loans.

### Modified Capabilities

## Impact

- New `Loan` aggregate, `LoanRepository` port, three use cases, `LoanController`, in-memory adapter.

# Spec Delta

## Purpose

Records which member holds which copy of a book, until when, and when it came back.

## ADDED Requirements

### Requirement: Lend a book
The system SHALL lend a book to a member for 21 days when at least one copy is not on loan and the member has fewer
open loans than the member's borrowing limit; otherwise it SHALL refuse the loan.

#### Scenario: Book is lent
- **WHEN** member m-1 borrows ISBN 9780132350884 on 2026-10-01 and a copy is available
- **THEN** a loan is open with due date 2026-10-22

#### Scenario: No copy available
- **WHEN** every copy of a book is on loan and a member asks to borrow it
- **THEN** the loan is refused with a no-copy-available error

#### Scenario: Member at the limit
- **WHEN** a member with 3 open loans asks to borrow a fourth book
- **THEN** the loan is refused with a borrowing-limit error

### Requirement: Return a book
The system SHALL close an open loan when the book is returned, recording the return date, and SHALL refuse to return
a loan that is already closed.

#### Scenario: Book is returned
- **WHEN** the loan is returned on 2026-10-10
- **THEN** the loan is closed with return date 2026-10-10 and the copy is available again

#### Scenario: Loan returned twice
- **WHEN** a closed loan is returned again
- **THEN** the request fails with an already-returned error

### Requirement: List a member's loans
The system SHALL list the open loans of a member with ISBN, loan date and due date.

#### Scenario: Open loans listed
- **WHEN** member m-1 has one open and one returned loan
- **THEN** only the open loan is listed

# sdd-library-loans

A small library-loans service (hexagonal, TypeScript, no runtime dependencies) built in five OpenSpec changes by a
coding agent that checked every implementation step with the DaedalusArch MCP tools. It is an illustration of
spec-driven development with an architecture checker in the loop, not an experiment. The write-up is
`Docs/v1.3/sdd-demo.md` in the repository root.

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `openspec/` | OpenSpec 1.14.0 project: `specs/` (five capabilities) and `changes/archive/` (the five changes: proposal, spec delta, design, tasks) |
| `.daedalus/architecture.yaml` | The DaedalusArch spec, generated from the `## Architecture` sections of the designs by `scripts/sdd/openspec-to-aac.ts` |
| `src/` | The service: `domain/`, `application/` (use cases, ports), `adapters/inbound/` (HTTP-style controllers), `adapters/scheduled/` (a daily job), `adapters/outbound/` (in-memory stores, clock, notifier), `config/` (composition root) |
| `scenarios.ts` | The 19 OpenSpec scenarios as executable checks |
| `transcript/transcript.jsonl` | Every file written, every derived spec, every MCP tool call with its result, every full evaluation, in order |
| `transcript/transcript.md` | The same, readable |

From the repository root:

```bash
npm ci
npm run demo:sdd                                    # rebuild from the transcript and re-check every step
npx tsx examples/sdd-library-loans/scenarios.ts     # run the scenarios
npx tsx scripts/sdd/openspec-to-aac.ts --project examples/sdd-library-loans \
  --out examples/sdd-library-loans/.daedalus/architecture.yaml --check
```
